subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Folding of a cell surface membrane (e.g. in the small intestine) speeds up absorption because it:
options: Increases the surface area for exchange
Adds more energy to the particles
questions.explain: Folds (villi/microvilli) increase surface area, increasing the rate of diffusion and active transport.

questions.q: Plant roots absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions by active transport because:
options: The ion concentration is higher in the soil than in the root
The ions must be moved against the concentration gradient into the root
The ions move down their concentration gradient
questions.explain: Mineral ions are usually more concentrated inside the root, so they must be moved against the gradient by active transport.

questions.q: Why does transpiration slow down when stomata close at night?
options: Water vapour can no longer escape easily through the closed pores
questions.explain: With stomata closed, water vapour cannot diffuse out, so transpiration slows.

questions.q: Which change would slow down the rate of diffusion of a substance into a cell?
options: Increasing the surface area of the membrane
questions.explain: A greater diffusion distance (a thicker barrier) reduces the rate of diffusion.

questions.q: Which statement about xylem is correct?
options: It is made of dead cells strengthened with lignin and carries water
It is made of living cells and carries sugars
It transports food in both directions
questions.explain: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes strengthened by lignin that carry water upwards.

questions.q: What is transpiration?
options: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant
The movement of sugars in phloem
questions.explain: Transpiration is the evaporation and loss of water vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.q: In an osmosis investigation, a potato chip GAINED mass. This shows the solution it was in was:
options: The same concentration as the cell contents
More concentrated than the cell contents
More dilute than the cell contents
questions.explain: Gaining mass means water entered by osmosis, so the surrounding solution was more dilute than the cell contents.

questions.q: Water moves into a cell by osmosis when the cell is surrounded by a solution with:
options: A lower water concentration than the cell
A higher water concentration than the cell
The same water concentration as the cell
questions.explain: Water moves from where there is more water (more dilute solution) into the cell.

questions.q: In osmosis, water moves from a region where it is:
options: More concentrated (dilute solution) to where it is less concentrated (concentrated solution)
Equally concentrated on both sides at all times
More concentrated to a more concentrated solution against the gradient
Less concentrated to more concentrated, using energy
questions.explain: Water moves from a dilute solution (high water concentration) to a concentrated solution (low water concentration) across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: How does mineral ion uptake by root hair cells usually occur?
options: By active transport against the concentration gradient
questions.explain: Mineral ions are taken into roots by active transport, which requires energy from respiration.

questions.q: The movement of sugars through phloem is called...
questions.explain: Translocation is the transport of dissolved food (sucrose) in the phloem.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: Moving air carries away water vapour, keeping a steep gradient and increasing transpiration.

questions.q: Why are xylem vessels strengthened with lignin?
options: To keep them hollow and support the plant
questions.explain: Lignin strengthens xylem vessels, keeping them open and helping support the plant.

questions.q: A cell placed in a concentrated salt solution loses water and shrinks. This is because water moves:
options: Into the cell by diffusion of salt
Out of the cell by active transport
Out of the cell by osmosis down its water gradient
questions.explain: The salt solution has a lower water concentration, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to estimate the rate of water uptake by a shoot?
questions.explain: A potometer measures water uptake, used to investigate transpiration rate.

questions.q: What is the main force that pulls water up through the xylem?
options: Evaporation of water from the leaves (transpiration pull)
questions.explain: Water evaporating from leaves creates a pull that draws water up the xylem.

questions.q: What does 'partially permeable' mean when describing a cell membrane in osmosis?
options: It lets water through but not larger solute molecules
It blocks water but allows large molecules through
It lets all substances pass through equally
It only allows movement when energy is supplied
questions.explain: A partially permeable membrane allows water molecules through but not larger solute molecules such as sugars.

questions.q: Why does increasing temperature usually increase transpiration?
options: Water molecules evaporate and diffuse faster
questions.explain: Higher temperatures speed up evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the leaf.

questions.q: Where does most water loss from a plant occur?
options: Through the stomata in the leaves
questions.explain: Most water is lost as vapour through the stomata in the leaves.

questions.q: In which direction(s) can phloem transport substances?
options: Both up and down the plant
questions.explain: Translocation in phloem can move dissolved food in both directions to where it is needed.

questions.q: Why does increased light intensity tend to increase transpiration?
options: Stomata open in the light for photosynthesis, allowing more water to escape
questions.explain: In light, stomata open to allow gas exchange for photosynthesis, so more water vapour is lost.

questions.q: Which condition would slow the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: High humidity reduces the concentration gradient of water vapour, slowing transpiration.
